Event_name: G7 Development Ministers' Meeting
Topics: Flood recovery; Climate finance; Development finance
Caption:
"Addressing the G7 Development Ministers' Meeting on the sidelines of #UNGA81, I drew the global community's attention to the recent Bhotekoshi disaster and the unimaginable loss it has caused.
The Bhotekoshi disaster is not just Nepal's tragedy; it is a stark warning from the Himalayas to the entire world. A warming planet can reverse decades of development gains in a matter of hours. Despite our negligible contribution to global emissions, we continue to bear the disproportionate and harsh impacts of climate change.
During the meeting, I outlined five key priorities for Nepal's effective recovery and reconstruction:
* Long-term Partnerships: Coordinated international efforts backed by grants and concessional financing for sustainable rebuilding.
* Accessible Climate Finance: Quick, simple, and direct access to financial resources, including the Loss and Damage Fund, for climate-vulnerable developing nations.
* Disaster Preparedness Investment: Scaling up support for early warning systems, climate information services, and community-based preparedness programs.
* Agile Multilateral Financing: Rapid and affordable financial mobilization through Multilateral Development Banks to serve as a lifeline against recurring climate shocks.
* Prioritizing the Himalayas: Placing the conservation of glaciers, water systems, and the Himalayan ecosystem at the very center of the global climate agenda.
I extend my deepest gratitude to the G7 members and all friendly nations for their strong solidarity and support during this difficult time. We must now translate international solidarity into concrete action, and shared responsibility into true climate justice. 🇳🇵🏔️🌍"

Event_name: High-level Event on Climate Action and the Just Transition
Topics: Climate; Flood recovery; Climate finance; Climate justice
About_UNGA_website: This Climate Summit, convened by UN Secretary-General António Guterres, will bring together leaders from major economies, developed and developing countries, vulnerable nations, and major energy producers and consumers to strengthen cooperation at a pivotal moment. Ten years after the Paris Agreement, the climate crisis has entered a new phase in which overshoot is now inevitable, while the energy transition accelerates. Leaders will take stock of progress and set out how they will work together to accelerate the transition, strengthen energy security, advance climate justice, and protect people from an accelerating climate crisis.
Caption:
"Addressing the High-Level Meeting on Climate Action and Just Transition at the UN Headquarters today, Hon. Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal made a strong and urgent appeal to the international community: it is time to decisively move from commitments to implementation. 🌍⚖️
Highlighting the recent devastating floods in Nepal—described as a "Himalayan Tsunami"—the Minister shared the grim reality of the disaster, which has caused over $5 billion in damages, equivalent to nearly 15% of the nation's GDP. Despite contributing less than 0.1% to global greenhouse gas emissions, Nepal continues to face the harsh and disproportionate impacts of a crisis it did not create.
The Minister emphasized that this is no longer just a humanitarian emergency; it is a development emergency, a crisis of justice, and an existential threat to frontline communities. Echoing the UN Secretary-General's previous warnings from the Himalayas, he reminded the world that "what happens in the Himalayas does not stay in the Himalayas." 🏔️🌊
Key calls to action included:
* Transitioning from fragmented, reactive aid to adequate, upfront, and easily accessible climate finance before disasters strike.
* Ensuring universal access to early warning systems, climate information services, and resilient infrastructure.
* Swift capitalization and simplified access to the Loss and Damage Fund.
* Mobilizing rapid and affordable financing through Multilateral Development Banks during crises.
* Holding the line on the 1.5°C temperature goal to ensure the survival of both mountain and coastal communities.
The Minister concluded with a powerful message to global leaders, civil society, and the private sector: "Climate action must be treated not as charity, but as justice." 🇳🇵

Link: High-level Event on Climate Action and the Just Transition"

Event_name: High-level Meeting to Commemorate the 40th Anniversary of the Declaration on the Right to Development
About_UNGA_website: Adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1986, the Declaration on the Right to Development  broke new ground in the universal struggle for greater human dignity, freedom, equality and justice. It called for every member of society to be empowered to participate fully and freely in vital decisions and demanded equal opportunities and the equitable distribution of economic resources. For the past four decades, the Declaration has provided a framework for advancing inclusive, sustainable, and participatory development at all levels, while shaping related laws and policies.

Event_name: Climate Vulnerable Forum (CVF) Leaders' Meeting
Topics: Climate; Flood recovery; Climate finance; Regional cooperation (SIDS)
Caption:
"ddressed the Climate Vulnerable Forum (CVF) Leaders' Meeting on the sidelines of #UNGA81 today, emphasizing the urgent need for stronger cooperation between mountainous nations and Small Island Developing States (SIDS). 🌍🏔️🏝️
Though geographically worlds apart—Nepal crowned by the world's highest peaks and Barbados surrounded by the Caribbean Sea—our ecological futures are deeply intertwined. From glacial lake outburst floods in the Himalayas to powerful hurricanes in the Caribbean, frontline communities are paying the ultimate price for global emissions they did not create.
During the address, outlined five key priorities to restructure the international development system and ensure true climate justice:
* Climate-Resilient Development: Ensuring all infrastructure investments can withstand climate risks and welcoming the rapid-response ‘Lifeline Fund’.
* Financial System Reform: Reforming development finance so climate disasters do not turn into debt crises, expressing strong support for the Bridgetown Initiative.
* Early Warning Systems: Expanding investment in science-based forecasting and real-time data sharing from the glaciers to the seas.
* Green & Digital Transformation: Accelerating a just transition to clean energy, with Nepal ready to contribute through clean hydropower.
* Effective Loss & Damage Financing: Securing new, grant-based resources for the Loss and Damage Fund—because repackaged commercial loans cannot adequately address the suffering caused by climate disasters.
Expressed deep appreciation for the leadership of Barbados Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley as CVF Chair. Reaffirmed Nepal's unwavering commitment to working alongside all CVF members to amplify our collective voice and secure a safe, sustainable future for generations to come. 🤝🇳🇵"

Event_name: 50th Annual Meeting of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs
Topics: UN reform; Development finance; Climate; Flood recovery; Regional cooperation
Caption:
“We call for timely reform of the international financial architecture, including greater voice and representation of developing countries in global economic governance.”

At #the Fiftieth Annual Meeting of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of Group of 77 and China at UNHQ on the margins of #UNGA81, Hon. Foreign Minister Mr. Shisir Khanal
stressed the need to renew solidarity and collective action to strengthen multilateralism, amplify the voice of the Global South, and advance a fairer and more inclusive world order.

He underscored strengthening a UN-centric rules-based multilateral; accelerating SDG action through adequate and affordable financing, technology transfer and capacity-building; and bridging inequalities through economic, digital transformation.

Highlighting the devastating impacts of Bhotekoshi flash floods, he called for climate justice with grant-based climate financing, and for stronger North-South, South-South and Triangular Cooperation to advance shared prosperity.

Event_name: “Sagarmatha to the Sea: A Call to Action for a Climate-Resilient Future”
Caption:
“The journey from Sagarmatha to the Sea, therefore, symbolizes the deep ecological interdependence of our planet and the shared destiny of humankind.”

In his concluding remarks at #Nepal’s High-Level Special Event “Sagarmatha to the Sea: A Call to Action for a Climate-Resilient Future” at UNHQ, Foreign Secretary Mr. Amrit Bahadur Rai stressed that intensifying climate crisis has posed an existential threat that transcends borders, ecosystems and generations.

He called for:

✅Climate finance must reach the most climate vulnerable countries and communities.

✅We must prioritize early warning and early action to reach people in time.

✅Climate risks must be integrated across development and disaster risk planning, guided by our collective commitments under the Paris Agreement, COP outcomes and the ICJ Advisory Opinion.

✅We must build stronger regional and international cooperation, deeper solidarity and enhanced climate diplomacy.

High-level Meeting to Mark the 25th Anniversary of the Adoption of the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action
Topics: Human rights; Anti-discrimination; Technology governance (AI); UN reform
About_UNGA_website: The Durban Declaration and Programme of Action is a global blueprint for racial justice and equality. Adopted at the 2001 World Conference Against Racism in South Africa, it laid the foundation for much of today’s international work against racial discrimination. Marking the 25th anniversary, this meeting serves as an opportunity to accelerate collective efforts to combat racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance under the theme: "Mobilizing global public support for the full and effective implementation of the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action."
Caption:
High-Level Meeting to Commemorate the 25th Anniversary of the Adoption of the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action #UNGA81

The High-level Meeting of the General Assembly to Commemorate #the Twenty-Fifth Anniversary of the Adoption of the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action on the theme of “Mobilizing global public support for the full and effective implementation of the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action” on the margins of #UNGA81.

Hon. Foreign Minister Mr. Khanal highlighted that the Durban Declaration reflects a common resolve of the international community to confront racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia, and enduring legacies of colonialism, apartheid, and systemic injustice.

He therefore called for enforcing legal and civic action on anti-discrimination laws; empowering marginalized communities; regulating emerging technologies including AI to eliminate racial algorithms and hate speech; and advancing principled multilateralism to do away with systemic intolerance worldwide.
